_comment: Run template for nist-heatpump-fdd: deliberately NO rules. The data are residential split heat pumps in a laboratory, one row per steady-state test point on a synthetic clock, and CAMBER has no detector that fits that equipment: the refrigerant-side drift family (subcooling, superheat, head / suction pressure, approach) is written for water-cooled chillers and needs a chilled-water load (flow and supply / return temperatures) this equipment does not have, and every time-based rule would read the synthetic clock as time. Mapping air-side temperatures or airflow onto chilled-water roles to make those rules run would misrepresent the equipment, so the template runs nothing and a `camber run` on it reports no findings. Use the ingested store to inspect the labelled fault signatures (e.g. subcooling 8.2 F fault-free vs 2.7 F at 80% charge and 18.5 F at 110.6% on the 14 SEER unit, long line set) and as validation data for a future heat-pump refrigerant-side or discharge-superheat detector (GitHub issue #6).
